public_rationale: CNBC reports $8 billion of cash burn in 2025, consistent with the first amount at the reported precision. That does not settle cumulative burn through 2030. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule, and the final deadline remains ahead.
limitations: The 2025 result comes from anonymous-source reporting.
The combined claim cannot receive a complete outcome from its elapsed component alone.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI will burn $8 billion or more in 2025 and, if his estimates are right, nearly a trillion dollars by 2030.

statement.excerpt: ChatGPT’s popularity — and OpenAI’s hunger for endless amounts of compute — have created the illusion of demand due to the sheer amount of capacity required to keep their services operational, all so they can burn $8 billion or more in 2025 and, if my estimates are right, nearly a trillion dollars by 2030.

our_interpretation: Burn means net cash consumed, rather than revenue, accounting losses, gross spending or announced commitments.
The statement contains two tests: calendar-year 2025 cash burn and cumulative cash burn through December 31, 2030. Both must hold to support the whole claim.
I read the cumulative window as 2025–2030, but its starting date is not explicit. The single metric_scope describes that combined window.
'If my estimates are right' expresses uncertainty about the estimate. It is not an independently observable antecedent that must occur before the forecast can be tested.
'Nearly' supplies no numerical tolerance. I do not impose one while the deadline remains outstanding.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable actual cash-flow evidence establishes at least $8 billion burned in 2025 and cumulative burn close to $1 trillion by the end of 2030.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable actual evidence establishes less than $8 billion burned in 2025, or completed-period cumulative burn clearly inconsistent with nearly $1 trillion.
